## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vedanāttika* (Patthana 13.2) is a section of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh and final treatise of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Within the Abhidhamma *mātikā* matrix, the *Vedanā-ttika* constitutes the "Triad of feelings" (phenomena associated with pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling), here subjected to systematic conditional analysis [Nyanatiloka 2007]. No independent translation exists for this specific sub-book on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

According to DharmaNexus, the text exhibits extensive Pali-internal reuse (1,234 matches shared across 83 Pali texts) [DharmaNexus]. Its largest shared passages occur with other Paṭṭhāna treatments of the feeling triad and root conditions, including *Vedanāttika* (Patthana 1.3; 39,998 shared characters), *Kusalattika, Vedanāttika* (Patthana 11.1; 28,050 shared characters), *Hetuduka, Tika* (Patthana 3.1; 23,824 shared characters), *Tika Hetuduka* (Patthana 4.1), and *Vedanāttika, Kusalattika* (Patthana 11.10) [DharmaNexus]. Outside the *Paṭṭhāna*, notable textual reuse appears with the *Vibhaṅga*, particularly the *Khandhavibhaṅga* (Vb 1) and the *Dhammahadayavibhaṅga* (Vb 18) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records low-scoring automatic cross-language alignments with the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26, fascicle 58) and the Tibetan translation of the *Yogācārabhūmi* (D 4035), though these reflect machine-detected phrase reuse rather than established historical parallels [DharmaNexus].
